intro: ほど is a measuring stick: it marks the degree something reaches. After a number it means "about that much"; after a clause it means "so much that ..."; in ほど～ない it holds up a standard that something fails to reach; and in ～ば～ほど the degree grows with each step.

skills.rule: Xほど sets the degree: after an amount it means "about X", after a clause it means "so much that X".
skills.explain:
After a number and counter, ほど means "about": 五分ほど待ってください. It is a slightly more formal くらい and is used for amounts and durations only. For a point on the clock use ごろ: 三時ごろ, never 三時ほど.

After a verb or adjective in plain form, ほど states how far something goes by naming a result: 涙が出るほど笑った, "I laughed so much that tears came". Fixed exaggerations are common: 死ぬほど疲れた, 信じられないほどおいしい. The ほど phrase sits in front of the word it measures, the opposite of English "so ... that".

くらい can replace ほど in both uses with little change. The difference shows at the low end: to belittle ("that little bit", "at least") only くらい works: それくらい自分でやって. ほど leans towards high, impressive degrees. まで after a clause means "until", not "to the degree".
patterns: [plain verb / adjective] ほど [adjective / verb]  "so ... that"
死ぬほど / 信じられないほど [adjective]

examples.jp: 五分[ごふん]{ほど}待[ま]ってください。
駅[えき]まで歩[ある]いて十分[じゅっぷん]{ほど}です。
examples.en: It's about a ten-minute walk to the station.

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は死[し]ぬ{ほど}疲[つか]れました。
涙[なみだ]が出[で]る{ほど}笑[わら]いました。
examples.en: I laughed so hard I cried.

examples.jp: この料理[りょうり]は信[しん]じられない{ほど}おいしいです。

contrast.note: Interchangeable for "about" and "so ... that", and more casual. Only くらい works for a low, belittling degree: それくらいできる, "I can manage that much".
まで is a limit in time or space, "until / as far as": 泣くまで is "until I cried". ほど measures how strongly, not how long.
だけ means "only": 五分だけ is "only five minutes", a cap, while 五分ほど is a rough estimate.

mistakes.bad: 三時[さんじ]{ほど}に来[き]てください。
mistakes.good: 三時[さんじ]{ごろ}に来[き]てください。
mistakes.note: ほど measures amounts; a point on the clock takes ごろ.

mistakes.bad: それ{ほど}自分[じぶん]でやってよ。
mistakes.good: それ{くらい}自分[じぶん]でやってよ。
mistakes.note: "Do that little bit yourself" belittles the task; only くらい carries the low "at least" sense.

skills.tip: Can you say "so much that" or "about" (of an amount) in English? Then ほど. Clock time is ごろ; "until" is まで.

skills.rule: AはBほど～ない means "A is not as ... as B"; the predicate must be negative.
skills.explain:
Put the standard of comparison before ほど and make the predicate negative: 今日は昨日ほど寒くない, "today is not as cold as yesterday". The topic (A) is the thing you are describing; B is the yardstick it falls short of. The pattern implies that B really is cold.

The standard can be a clause: 思ったほど難しくなかった, "it wasn't as hard as I thought". それほど / そんなに～ない means "not that ...": それほど高くない. With a noun phrase and ものはない / 人はいない it means "nothing is as ... as": 母の料理ほどおいしいものはない.

In this comparison ほど needs a negative predicate. "A is colder than B" is AはBより寒い; "A is as cold as B" is AはBと同じくらい寒い. Do not mix up より and ほど: より marks what A exceeds, ほど marks what A fails to reach. しか～ない is a different pattern meaning "only".
patterns: A は B ほど [adjective / verb] ない
[plain verb] ほど ～ない  "not as ... as I expected"
B ほど [adjective] もの / 人 は ない / いない

examples.jp: 今日[きょう]は昨日[きのう]{ほど}寒[さむ]くないです。
examples.en: Today isn't as cold as yesterday.

examples.jp: それ{ほど}高[たか]くないですよ。
私[わたし]の部屋[へや]は兄[あに]の部屋[へや]{ほど}広[ひろ]くありません。
examples.en: My room isn't as big as my brother's.

examples.jp: テストは思[おも]った{ほど}難[むずか]しくなかった。
examples.en: The test wasn't as hard as I thought.

examples.jp: 母[はは]の料理[りょうり]{ほど}おいしいものはありません。
examples.en: Nothing is as delicious as my mother's cooking.

contrast.note: AはBより暑い: A goes beyond B (affirmative). AはBほど暑くない: A falls short of B. より is "more than", ほど～ない is "not as ... as".
しか～ない means "only": 東京しか知らない, "I only know Tokyo". It does not compare.
Fine in "nothing is as ... as" (田中さんくらい優しい人はいない), but for plain "not as ... as" ほど is the standard choice.

mistakes.bad: 今日[きょう]は昨日[きのう]{ほど}暑[あつ]いです。
mistakes.good: 今日[きょう]は昨日[きのう]{より}暑[あつ]いです。
mistakes.note: ほど needs a negative predicate. For "hotter than" use より.

mistakes.bad: テストは思[おも]った{ほど}難[むずか]しかった。
mistakes.good: テストは思[おも]った{より}難[むずか]しかった。
mistakes.note: An affirmative predicate rules out ほど. "Harder than I thought" is 思ったより; 思ったほど needs 難しくなかった.

skills.tip: See ない at the end of a comparison? The yardstick takes ほど. No ない, it takes より.

skills.rule: Xば Xほど means "the more X, the more ...": say the same word in its ば form, then in its plain form plus ほど.
skills.explain:
Repeat one verb or adjective: first the ば conditional, then the plain form with ほど. 練習すればするほど上手になる, "the more you practise, the better you get". The second half states what changes in step: なる, 増える, an adjective, or いい in 早ければ早いほどいい, "the sooner the better".

Forms: verbs 読めば読むほど, する verbs 練習すればするほど; い-adjectives 安ければ安いほど; な-adjectives 静かなら静かなほど. The plain form before ほど never takes ば again.

The ば half may be dropped with no change of meaning: 勉強するほど面白くなる. Plain ～ば alone is only a condition ("if you practise, you will improve") with no sense of scale. より compares two fixed things and cannot express this growth.
patterns: [い-adj ければ] [same adj] ほど
[な-adj なら] [same adj な] ほど

examples.jp: 早[はや]ければ早[はや]い{ほど}いいです。
練習[れんしゅう]すればする{ほど}上手[じょうず]になります。
examples.en: The more you practise, the better you get.

examples.jp: この本[ほん]は読[よ]めば読[よ]む{ほど}面白[おもしろ]い。
examples.en: The more you read this book, the more interesting it gets.

examples.jp: 部屋[へや]は静[しず]かなら静[しず]かな{ほど}いいです。
examples.en: The quieter the room, the better.

examples.jp: 考[かんが]えれば考[かんが]える{ほど}わからなくなる。
examples.en: The more I think about it, the less I understand.

examples.jp: 日本語[にほんご]は勉強[べんきょう]する{ほど}面白[おもしろ]くなります。
examples.en: The more you study Japanese, the more interesting it becomes.

contrast.note: より compares two fixed things (今日は昨日より暑い). It cannot express "the more ..., the more ...".
練習すれば上手になる is a plain condition: "if you practise, you'll improve". Adding するほど turns it into a scale.

mistakes.bad: 安[やす]いば安[やす]い{ほど}いいです。
mistakes.good: 安[やす]ければ安[やす]い{ほど}いいです。
mistakes.note: The ば form of an い-adjective is ～ければ: 安ければ.

mistakes.bad: 練習[れんしゅう]すればすれば{ほど}上手[じょうず]になります。
mistakes.good: 練習[れんしゅう]すればする{ほど}上手[じょうず]になります。
mistakes.note: Only the first half takes ば; the word before ほど is plain: するほど.

mistakes.bad: 練習[れんしゅう]すればする{より}上手[じょうず]になります。
mistakes.good: 練習[れんしゅう]すればする{ほど}上手[じょうず]になります。
mistakes.note: "The more ..., the more" is ほど; より only compares.

skills.tip: Hear the same word twice, ば then plain? The slot after it is ほど.
